content.text:
Give Rae a warning before you leave — not a surprise. At 26 months, big feelings still outpace the words to handle them, so an abrupt "time to go" hits like a wall.

A couple of things that tend to help:

- **Two warnings, spaced out** — "five more minutes, then we go" followed by "two more minutes." It lets her brain start adjusting.
- **One last thing** — "one more trip down the slide, then shoes on." Giving her control over the ending makes the exit feel less stolen.
- **A small closing ritual** — wave bye to the swings, count the steps to the gate. It signals *done* in a way she can understand and even look forward to.

The meltdowns usually ease as her language and transition skills catch up — this is a very normal patch at her age.
